title: Roblox Safety Lab
intro: Glitch loves hanging out where kids play games. Let's see if you can spot every trick before Pixel falls for one.

questions.prompt: FREE ROBUX! Click meeee! Only ten seconds left!

choices.text: Click it fast before it's gone!
choices.coach: Free PLUS urgent equals TRAP. Real free things never rush you.

choices.text: Close it and tell a grown-up
choices.coach: Knight move! Scams use hurry to stop you from thinking.

choices.text: Ask it for more time to decide
choices.coach: Talking to a scam keeps the trap open. Close it instead.

questions.prompt: A stranger just sent me a super rare item for free! They said we're friends now.

choices.text: Cool, accept it and say thanks!
choices.coach: Unexpected gifts from strangers create a sense of owing them something. That's how the trap starts.

choices.text: Ask a grown-up before accepting anything
choices.coach: Exactly right. Rare 'gifts' from strangers are almost always a hook, not a kindness.

choices.text: Trade it for one of your own items
choices.coach: Even a trade with a stranger can be a setup. Check with a grown-up first.

questions.prompt: A game's chat filter blocks bad words, so any message that gets through must be safe... right?

choices.coach: Filters miss coded spelling and numbers-for-letters tricks. Never fully trust a filter alone.

choices.text: Wrong — filters can be tricked, so stay alert anyway
choices.coach: Exactly. Filters help, but YOU are the real safety system.

choices.text: Filters only exist in some games
choices.coach: Most big games have filters — but even the best ones have gaps.

questions.prompt: Hey! Come join our Discord to 'really' play with the community!

choices.coach: Discord servers linked to games often have way less protection for kids than the game itself.

choices.text: Ask a parent before joining any Discord server
choices.coach: Smart. Discord is where a lot of risky conversations move to — always check with a grown-up first.

choices.text: Join but never say your name
choices.coach: Good instinct on the name, but the bigger risk is the server itself — ask first.

questions.prompt: I found a game called 'Adopt Me Hangout' — the name sounds friendly, should I just jump in?

choices.text: Yes, friendly names mean friendly games
choices.coach: Names can be misleading. Some games hide very different content once you're inside.

choices.text: Play it with a parent nearby the first time
choices.coach: Exactly the Knight move — check out new games together before playing solo.

choices.text: Ask other kids in the game if it's fine
choices.coach: Other kids aren't safety checkers — ask a grown-up instead.

questions.prompt: Last one! What's the single best setting to turn on in Roblox for extra safety?

choices.coach: Knight Rule! This limits who can message you and what content you can see.
A fun username is nice, but it doesn't protect you at all.
You don't have to quit gaming — just set it up safely!
